<!-- Generated by internal/tools/docgen from the cobra command tree. DO NOT EDIT: run `make docs-reference`. -->

Follows new events as they arrive (like tail -f). Every --interval it polls for
events in the last --window. Events are sorted within each poll but not across
polls, so an event that arrives more than one window late prints out of order.

:::tip[Learn more]
The Bronto docs explain the platform concept behind this command: [docs.bronto.io/Search-and-Visualize/Log-Search](https://docs.bronto.io/Search-and-Visualize/Log-Search)
:::

```sh
bronto tail [query] [flags]
```

#### Flags

| Flag | Short | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--dataset` | `-d` | stringArray |  | dataset name or UUID to tail (repeatable) |
| `--dedup-size` |  | int | `20000` | number of recent events remembered to drop duplicates across polls; raise it for very high-volume streams |
| `--exclude` |  | stringArray |  | hide lines matching this regex (repeatable) |
| `--from-expr` |  | string |  | dataset selector expression |
| `--group-by` | `-g` | stringArray |  | group-by key for live aggregates (repeatable; switches to aggregate mode) |
| `--highlight` |  | stringArray |  | highlight regex matches in the output (repeatable) |
| `--include` |  | stringArray |  | only show lines matching this regex (repeatable, ANDed) |
| `--interval` |  | duration | `3s` | polling interval (min 1s) |
| `--limit` | `-n` | int | `500` | max events per poll |
| `--no-follow` |  | bool |  | fetch the current window once and exit |
| `--select` |  | stringArray |  | aggregate to compute on each poll, e.g. count(\*) (repeatable; switches to aggregate mode) |
| `--window` |  | string | `30s` | per-poll lookback window (single unit) |

Also accepts the [global flags](/reference/commands/global-flags/).

#### Examples

```sh
bronto tail
bronto tail "level = 'error'" --include 'timeout' --exclude 'healthz'
bronto tail --no-follow --window 5m   # catch up, then exit
bronto tail -g status --window 1m     # live count(*) by status, redrawn in place
```
